h: A Grim Corner of the City With Great Neighbours
p: The York Dungeon is on Clifford Street, in the old heart of the city, and that location is a gift for planning the rest of the day. Clifford's Tower, the surviving stone keep of York Castle, is a few minutes' walk away, and the York Castle Museum next to it recreates a Victorian street that's a cracking contrast to the Dungeon's horrors. JORVIK Viking Centre in Coppergate is close by too, so you can see the Vikings told straight after you've seen them told for laughs.

York's centre is compact and best explored on foot. Park and ride services save the stress of hunting for spaces in the medieval streets, and the station is an easy walk away if you're coming by train. Walking a stretch of the city walls is free and gives you a different view of the rooftops and the Minster.

Inside the Dungeon, comfy shoes and small bags make life easier, as you'll be on your feet and moving through tight, dark spaces. Arrive a little before your slot and use the loo first, as once the group sets off there's no hanging about. Keen to steal the show? Stand near the front. Prefer a quiet life? Hide behind the tallest person in your group and hope for the best.
Weekends and school holidays fill up fast, so book in advance.
